item.title: Trump Administration Pressures California With Expanded Voter Fraud Investigation
item.description: The department has issued grand jury subpoenas to local election officials as part of a widening effort to prove unsubstantiated claims about large numbers of illegal voters in the state.
item.dc:creator: Devlin Barrett and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Voters casting their ballots in Los Angeles in June. At least two employees of Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder’s office received grand jury subpoenas last week.

item.title: Republicans Ramp Up Investigation Into Democratic Plan to Pack Alaska’s Ballot
item.description: The Justice Department issued subpoenas, a House oversight committee sought interviews and the state opened its own inquiry into a Democratic plan to recruit a spoiler into a Senate race.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning, Anna Griffin and Glenn Thrush
item.media:description: Republican anger grew on Thursday over a Democratic effort to stack Alaska’s Senate ballot with candidates to siphon votes from the G.O.P. incumbent.

item.title: Trump Cancels Rallies in Kansas and Iowa This Weekend
item.description: President Trump has been holding hours-long rallies for G.O.P. candidates nearly every day for weeks.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: President Trump at Joint Base Andrews, Md., after a campaign rally in South Carolina.

item.title: How Common Is Ballot Stacking? What to Know as Conflict Roils Alaska Senate Race.
item.description: As a conflict over candidates roils the Alaskan Senate race, here’s a look back at the political practice over the years.
item.dc:creator: Madison Malone Kircher
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times; Christopher Miller for The New York Times

item.title: No Clear Winner in Israel Election, Final Results Show
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party and its allies won 53 seats in Parliament, falling short of the outright majority needed to form a government. The main opposition bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, won 48.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands, Johnatan Reiss and Ephrat Livni

item.title: What Israeli Election Results Reveal About the Electorate
item.description: Some groups stood by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party, but support fell off among others. Turnout was also a striking factor in the election.
item.dc:creator: Johnatan Reiss
item.media:description: Election campaign posters for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party in Adora, an Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, on Tuesday.

item.title: Polymarket Is Investigating Suspicious Bets on Israeli Election
item.description: The company said it was looking into hundreds of new accounts that had placed wagers in two markets related to the election on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy and Stuart A. Thompson
item.media:description: Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, speaking at a Likud event in Jerusalem on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump Erupted After Learning of Alina Habba’s $50 Million Deal
item.description: Angry about the scale of a contract signed by one of his former lawyers with the family of a wealthy pardon seeker, the president told allies he wanted some of the money to go to his future presidential library.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Pager
item.category: Trump, Donald J, Presidential Library and Museum
item.media:description: Alina Habba Mildon, while working as an adviser at the Justice Department, had signed on last year to serve as a general counsel for a company started by the daughter of Julio Herrera Velutini, who was seeking a pardon.

item.title: Patrick Stewart, ‘Star Trek’ Captain and Professor X on ‘X-Men,’ Dies at 86
item.description: The British actor was 86. He achieved pop-culture stardom as Capt. Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek: The Next Generation.”
item.dc:creator: Anita Gates and William McDonald
item.category: Star Trek: The Next Generation (TV Program)
item.media:credit: Ryan Pfluger for The New York Times
item.media:description: Patrick Stewart was Professor X in five “X-Men” movies, Macbeth on Broadway and, recently, the voice of a wise ram in “The Sheep Detectives.”

item.title: Patrick Stewart Brought Elegance To ‘Star Trek’ as Jean-Luc Picard
item.description: Led by the Shakespearean veteran in his role as Jean-Luc Picard, “Star Trek: The Next Generation” gracefully went where the franchise had never gone before.
item.dc:creator: Sopan Deb
item.category: Star Trek: The Next Generation (TV Program)
item.media:description: Patrick Stewart was initially uncertain whether he should play Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” but it became his signature role.

item.title: Patrick Stewart’s Many Roles, From ‘Star Trek’ to ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
item.description: The actor’s long and varied career included Shakespearean roles, “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” comedy and a stint in the Marvel Universe.
item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.category: Star Trek: The Next Generation (TV Program)
item.media:credit: NBC, Sara Krulwich/The New York Times, Fox, Kerry Hayes/20th Century Fox, CBS via Getty Images, Sesame Street Workshop
item.media:description: Patrick Stewart has played many memorable roles.

item.title: Newly Freed American Describes His Years in Russian Prison
item.description: Stephen James Hubbard, the retired teacher arrested soon after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, said he sometimes lost hope.
item.dc:creator: Kim Barker
item.media:description: Stephen James Hubbard with relatives and U.S. officials aboard a flight to the United States after his release from Russian prison, in a photo released by the U.S. government.

item.title: Rare Evacuation Announced by Melania Trump Begins in Ukrainian City of Oleshky
item.description: Many people left in Oleshky, where bombardment is constant, have run out of food. A truce that began Tuesday is supposed to allow aid in and civilians out.
item.dc:creator: Carlotta Gall and Oleksandr Chubko
item.media:description: An apartment building, damaged by Russian attacks in Oleshky, Ukraine.

item.title: Big Tech’s Data Center Blitz Is Burning Through Cash and Scaring Wall St.

item.dc:creator: Karen Weise

item.title: Intel’s Shares Plunge 20% as A.I. Hinders Some Parts of Its Business
item.description: The chipmaker, whose largest investor is the U.S. government, reported that the A.I. boom’s domino effect had hurt sales to personal computer makers.
item.dc:creator: Don Clark
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: A silicon wafer at Intel’s campus in Ocotillo, Ariz. The company reported revenue of $16.5 billion in its third quarter.

item.title: Binance Grapples With ‘Security Incident’ That May Cause $6.3 Billion in Losses
item.description: The world’s largest crypto exchange suspended deposits and withdrawals after an apparent hack.
item.dc:creator: David Yaffe-Bellany
item.media:description: Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder, said the incident “does look like a hack.”

item.title: How a Self-Described ‘Junkie’ Rode Synthetic Drugs to Oblivion — and Fame
item.description: An Estonian addict could barely keep pace with the new drugs flooding the market. His terrifying accounts of the cruel toll they took on his body held his country in its grip.
item.dc:creator: Azam Ahmed
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Estonian police used to respond to reports of people sniffing glue at these abandoned housing units. Now ultra-potent new synthetic drugs are keeping them busy.

item.title: Cuba’s Foreign Minister: We’ll Outlast Trump

item.media:description: Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla of Cuba during an interview with The New York Times this week.

item.title: U.S. Expels Cuban Diplomat After Fiery Showdown at United Nations
item.description: Tensions have risen between the United States and Cuba as the Trump administration tries to force the island’s Communist government to make drastic changes.
